title: The mode of that Spirit-work is obscure, though every believer experiences the faith
pass_a_gloss: But what the mode of that operation is, is a matter very obscure and hard to explain — which might perhaps seem strange to someone. For since that operation of the Holy Spirit takes place in our souls, we seem to ought to know it by sense itself and experience. Yet there is nothing in this that we ought to wonder at. For we experience many things in ourselves, and indeed we ourselves perform many things, whose reason and mode we nevertheless do not grasp and are not able to understand. So every day we experience that we see and understand, and yet when it must be explained how vision and intellection take place, the sharpest and most learned men stick fast and cannot sufficiently disentangle themselves. And there is still a dispute among physicists and mathematicians whether vision happens by the emission of rays or by the reception of visible species. Therefore, although every believer experiences that he embraces God's Word with certain faith and gives full and firm assent to sacred Scripture, it ought not to move wonder if theologians stick fast in explaining how that faith is generated in us, and by what reason the Spirit brings forth that assent in us. On which matter we will briefly set out our opinion.
pass_b_english: But what the mode of that operation is remains very obscure and hard to explain — which might seem strange. Since the Holy Spirit's work happens in our souls, we seem as if we ought to know it by sense and experience itself. Yet there is nothing odd here. We experience many things in ourselves, and we ourselves do many things, whose reason and mode we still do not grasp and cannot understand.

Every day we experience that we see and understand; yet when someone must explain how vision and intellection happen, the sharpest and most learned men stick fast and cannot disentangle themselves. Physicists and mathematicians still dispute whether vision happens by the emission of rays or by the reception of visible species.

So although every believer experiences that he embraces God's Word with certain faith and gives full, firm assent to sacred Scripture, it should not surprise us if theologians stick fast when they try to explain how that faith is generated in us, and how the Spirit brings forth that assent. On that we will briefly set out our view.
source_text: VI. Quis sit autem istius operationis modus, res valde obscura est et explicatu difficilis: quod forte cuipiam mirum videri posset. Cum enim illa Spiritus sancti operatio in animis nostris fiat, videmur id nosse debere sensu ipso et experientia. Sed tamen in eo nihil est quod mirari debeamus. Etenim multa in nobis experimur, imo multa operamur ipsi, quorum tamen rationem et modum non tenemus, nec valemus intelligere. Sic quotidie experimur nos videre et intelligere, et tamen, quum explicandum est qua ratione visio et intellectio fiat, acutissimi quique et doctissimi viri haerent, nec satis possunt se expedire. Et adhuc lis est inter Physicos et Mathematicos, An visio fiat per radiorum emissionem, An vero per receptionem specierum visibilium. Igitur etsi fidelis quisque experiatur se verbum Dei certa fide amplecti, plenumque et firmum assensum Scripturae sacrae tribuere, admirationem movere non debet, si Theologi haereant in exponendo, quomodo fides illa nobis ingeneretur, et qua ratione Spiritus assensum illum in nobis pariat. Qua de re sententiam nostram breviter exponemus.
